Errors raised by transitmattr

Source: R/errors.R
transitmattr_errors.Rd

When a request fails, transitmattr raises an error with one of these classes, so you can handle each kind of failure with tryCatch():

Details

transitmattr_error
|-- transitmattr_http_error       the API responded with an error status
|   |-- transitmattr_bad_request    400: a parameter is missing or invalid
|   |-- transitmattr_range_too_long 403: the date range has too many entries
|   |-- transitmattr_not_found      404: no route has this ID
|   `-- transitmattr_server_error   5xx: the API failed
`-- transitmattr_network_error    no response: a timeout or failed connection

HTTP errors have fields status (the HTTP status code), code (the error type the API reported, such as "ForbiddenError", or NULL), and content (the response body as text). They also have httr2's classes httr2_http_<status>, httr2_http, and httr2_error, so handlers written for earlier versions keep working.

Requests that time out, fail to connect, or get a 429, 502, 503, or 504 response are retried up to three times before an error is raised.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
tryCatch(
  tm_stops("Purple"),
  transitmattr_not_found = function(e) {
    message("No such route: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
} # }
